page: Vultr voc-g-8c-32gb-160s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical AMD EPYC cores with multithreading enabled. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, the x86_64 architecture processor is paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via a 160 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU supports AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and BMI2 instruction sets, though it lacks AVX-512 extensions.

In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core results placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. Multi-core performance aligns with the middle 50% average, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 23301.5 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8841.0. Memory bandwidth is stable, recording 117.03 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 77.42 GB/sec for large block write operations. Database operations and web serving throughput are average, with Redis SET operations reaching 15.29 million operations per second and static web serving throughput measured at 8.45 GB/sec.

The primary performance tradeoff is observed in heavy computational tasks such as large language model inference. While prompt processing for a small 135M model is average at 656.07 tokens per second, processing a medium 7B model drops to a weak 18.38 tokens per second. Consequently, this instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including web serving, software compilation, database operations, and moderate multi-threaded applications, rather than intensive machine learning or large-scale LLM deployment. The dedicated AMD EPYC cores and NVMe storage provide a reliable, cost-efficient resource density for standard production environments.
